chunks: Your Lord knows you better: He may have mercy on you if He please, or punish you if He will. Yet We have not sent you as warden over them.

key_terms.يَرْحَمْكُمْ: He may have mercy on you

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between God's knowledge and His power to mercy or punish?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of divine omnipotence (Qudrah) and omniscience (Ilm), affirming that while the Prophet is a mercy to mankind, he is not an agent of compulsion (Mukallif) over individual souls. It highlights the balance between God's absolute authority to reward or punish and the Prophet's role as a witness rather than a controller, reinforcing the theological principle that guidance and misguidance ultimately rest with Allah's will.
